# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_007_page_001.jpg

---

**7:1** I am mortal, the same as everyone else. I descend from the first human being, shaped from the earth. I was made flesh in a mother's womb —

**7:2** ten months forming in blood, from a man's seed and the pleasure that belongs to sleep and marriage.

**7:3** When I was born, I breathed the same air as everyone else and fell on the same earth that receives us all. My first sound was a cry — like every other human being before or after me.

**7:4** I was wrapped in swaddling cloths and looked after with care.

**7:5** No king has ever come into the world any differently.

**7:6** There is one door in for all of us, and one door out.

**7:7** So I prayed — and understanding was given to me. I called out to God — and the spirit of wisdom came.

**7:8** I valued her above scepters and thrones. Beside her, wealth meant nothing.

**7:9** I would not compare her to any precious stone. All the gold in the world is a handful of sand next to her. Silver is just clay.

**7:10** I loved her more than I loved health. More than physical beauty. I chose her over light itself — because her light never goes out.

**7:11** Every good thing came to me with her. In her hands, wealth beyond counting.

**7:12** I was glad for all of it — because wisdom was what made it possible. What I didn't know yet was that she was the mother of it all.

**7:13** I learned without holding anything back. I share without holding anything back. I will not hoard her wealth.

**7:14** She is an inexhaustible treasure for all human beings. Those who draw from her treasury gain friendship with God — recommended to him by the gifts that wisdom's teaching brings.

**7:15** God, grant me to speak as the subject deserves, and to think thoughts that honor what I have been given — because it is he who guides wisdom, and he who keeps the wise from going wrong.

**7:16** We are in his hands. Everything we are. Every word we speak. Every thought we form. Every skill we possess.

**7:17** He gave me accurate knowledge of how things are: the structure of the universe, the operation of its elements;

**7:18** the beginning of time, its end, its turning points; the movements of the solstices, the rhythms of the seasons;

**7:19** the cycles of the years, the arrangement of the stars;

**7:20** the natures of animals, the instincts of wild things; the powers of spirits, the workings of human minds; the varieties of plants, the medicinal properties of roots.

**7:21** Everything hidden and everything visible — I came to know it all. Because wisdom, the maker of everything, taught me.

**7:22** In wisdom there is a spirit: intelligent, holy, unique, many-faceted, subtle, freely moving, lucid, beyond all stain, clear, beyond all harm, loving the good, sharp, unobstructed, beneficent, and a friend to all humanity.

**7:23** Steadfast, sure, undisturbed, all-powerful, all-seeing — a spirit that moves through all other spirits, however intelligent, pure, and subtle they may be.

**7:24** Wisdom is more mobile than any motion there is. Because of her absolute purity, she flows through and into all things.

**7:25** She is a breath from the power of God. She is a pure stream flowing out from the glory of the Almighty. Nothing contaminated can enter her.

**7:26** She is a radiance from the light that is eternal. A spotless mirror that reflects the energy of God. An image of his goodness.

**7:27** She is one — yet she can do all things. She stays entirely herself — yet she makes everything new. Age after age she moves into holy souls, making them friends of God, making them prophets.

**7:28** God loves nothing on earth so deeply as the person who lives with wisdom.

**7:29** She is more beautiful than the sun. She outshines every grouping of stars. Put her beside ordinary light — she wins.

**7:30** Night follows day without fail. But nothing — nothing in existence — overpowers wisdom.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Chapter 7 is the summit of the book. The personal opening (vv. 1–6) establishes Solomon's common humanity before his extraordinary gift. The 21 attributes (vv. 22–23) are rendered in a sustained list — no connectives artificially inserted. The key philosophical verses: 7:25 ("breath of the power of God" — atmis, the vapor/breath of divine power; aporroia — outflowing/emanation) and 7:26 ("reflection of eternal light" — apaugasma, later used in Heb 1:3 of Christ). The final verse's "nothing overpowers wisdom" is placed emphatically.*
